ledger.claim: The trip was a scheduled 21:15 pickup and the driver was still not there when the rider cancelled at 21:23:15. The trip record fixes the no-show deadline at 2026-08-19T21:20:00+08:00 and reports arrived_by_deadline = false with arrived_at null. Under POL-NS-24 the rider was therefore entitled to cancel at no charge from 21:20 onwards, and the 5.00 SGD charged to her must be refunded in full.

The GPS evidence independently confirms the driver never reached the pickup. The arrival check reports corroborated = false, arrived_at = null and nearest_fix = null against an arrival radius of 50 m for a STANDARD pickup zone, so no fix places the driver within the POL-NS-21 arrival radius at any point in the trace; the driver's actual position after 21:09:30 was not at the pickup. The driver-no-show condition in POL-NS-24 is thus established on both the trip record and the trace.

The driver stopped and stayed stopped through the whole of the scheduled time and the free-wait window. The last moving fix reports 11 kph at 21:09:00; each of the 28 fixes from 21:09:30 to 21:23:00 reports 0 kph, and the trace covers only 1.697 km in total. Nothing in the trace shows a final approach to the pickup between 21:09:30 and the rider's cancellation at 21:23:15. Because arrived_at is null, the POL-NS-21 free wait never even began to run for this driver — there was no arrival from which it could start.

The driver made no contact with the rider at all before the trip was cancelled. The trip record's contact_before_cancel block reports message_count = 0 and call_count = 0, with obligation_met = false; the chat log holds only the rider's two messages ('Hi, where are you? App shows you not moving' at 21:16:40 and 'Hello??' at 21:19:30); and the only in-app call in the record is the rider's own at 21:20:10, which the driver did not answer. Both limbs of POL-NS-23 fail. The rider cancelled only because the driver never appeared and never responded to her — the very situation that clause protects against — so the fee is voided with no driver compensation.

Because the driver not only failed to arrive but also failed to attempt any contact, POL-NS-24's second limb applies on top of the refund: a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is due to the rider. The fare ledger's money block carries goodwill_credit_sgd at 5.00. Under POL-GEN-03 that credit is a referral naming the clause, not an escalation, and it does not suppress the monetary outcome.

The driver's only account is 'Passenger cancel herself, why she complain. I was coming.' Nothing on this record supports it as a delayed approach. The traffic-data artifact for this trip, EV-ADVIS-05056-01, is MISSING: its admissibility status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it carries no fact and there is no advisory to explain any delay, whether inside or outside the free-wait window. The absence is citable and it counts against the driver, not the rider.

The money is straightforward and unmoved: the ledger shows cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, while the derived money block sets fee_charged_sgd and refund_if_voided_sgd both at 5.00. A ruling that voids the fee therefore moves exactly 5.00 SGD back to the filing rider — a FULL_REFUND as POL-GEN-03 defines it, with driver_compensation_sgd null because POL-NS-23 voids the fee 'with no driver compensation'.

There is nothing here for a human reviewer to resolve. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, and neither profile carries a fraud flag of 1 or more (both are 0), so the AI ruling is final at any confidence under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26. Every fact POL-NS-24 and POL-NS-23 need — the deadline, the non-arrival, the absence of contact — is established on complete, weight-1.0 artifacts, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged and the case should be decided on the merits in the rider's favour rather than held.

The 5.00 SGD on the ledger is exactly the policy figure: fee_charged_sgd 5.00, policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy true, and the driver's share of the fee is 1.00. POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show fee at 5.00 SGD and transfers it to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, so there is no amount error on this record and no arithmetic correction for any ruling to make; whatever the judge decides about entitlement, the number charged is the number the policy sets.

POL-NS-23 binds the driver only 'before cancelling for no-show'. The trip record shows the cancellation was the rider's, not the driver's: cancelled_by RIDER, cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED, and the trip_cancelled event at 21:23:15. The driver never cancelled, so the contact precondition in POL-NS-23 never engaged and the fee cannot be voided on that clause; the rider's point that the driver sent no message and placed no call is directed at a duty the clause raises only against a driver who cancels.

POL-NS-24 refunds the fee only where the driver 'fails to arrive at the pickup location', and that fact is not established on this record. The derived arrival block carries arrived_at null, nearest_fix null and accuracy_reported null, and its corroborated value is false only because the category's arrival test corroborates a trip-record arrival event and this trip record logs none; the trace is never used in the derived facts to measure the vehicle's distance from the pickup at 21:20. Where a fact a rule needs is not carried by the attached evidence, POL-GEN-26 sends the open question to a human reviewer. I do not assert that the record shows the driver at the pickup; I say it shows neither, and that an unresolved arrival question is not a licence to refund the fee.

The driver's device reported continuously for the whole life of this trip: 49 fixes at 30 s intervals, coverage 100%, no gap above 30 s, 1.697 km driven after acceptance, the vehicle stationary from 21:09:30 and the last fix at 21:23:00, fifteen seconds before the rider's own cancellation at 21:23:15. The driver never ended the trip and was still live on it when the rider cancelled; the time and the fuel that POL-NS-22's fee compensates were in fact spent on this booking.

No traffic data was attached for this trip. EV-ADVIS-05056-01 is MISSING, carries issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, and so carries no fact (POL-GEN-02); the record therefore holds no third-party account of conditions on the driver's approach between 20:58 and 21:23, and the completeness of the account of why the approach took as long as it did is not something this record can settle. Where a fact the rules need is not carried by any attached evidence, POL-GEN-26 directs that the question go to a human reviewer with the amount held, not that the fee be refunded.

If the fee stands, POL-NS-22 and POL-GEN-03 require the ruling to be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the 5.00 SGD charged, that figure being the money the ruling moves and not a second payment. In the alternative the present state stands as NO_ACTION: the charge is live (payment_status CHARGED) and no refund has issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and on this record the rider has not established the ground that would take the 5.00 SGD back.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged to the rider is refunded in full.

Why. This was a scheduled 21:15 pickup. Under POL-NS-24 the driver had to be at the pickup by 21:20 (the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, the free wait POL-NS-21 fixes), after which the rider could cancel at no charge. He was not there. The trip record logs no arrival at all (arrived_at null, arrived_by_deadline false against the 21:20:00 deadline), and the driver's own device trace - complete, 100% coverage, 49 fixes at 30-second intervals, no gap over 30 seconds, weight 1.0 - shows the vehicle stationary from 21:09:30 through the last fix at 21:23:00 and never inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup. The rider cancelled at 21:23:15, after the deadline, and the 5.00 SGD fee was charged at 21:23:19 and is still live (total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Any fee charged in this situation is refunded in full: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, read off the fare ledger's cancellation_fee and refund_if_voided_sgd of 5.00.

The driver's answer, that the arrival fact is not established because the arrival check reports corroborated false and nearest_fix null, is rejected. Those nulls arise because there is no trip-record arrival event to corroborate; they do not put the vehicle at the pickup. POL-NS-24 reads the trip record and the trace together, and the trace is not impaired over the window that matters, so its result decides, in either direction - and it shows a driver who stopped short of the pickup and stayed stopped through the deadline.

The driver is right that POL-NS-23 does not engage on its own terms: its precondition is a driver cancelling for no-show, and the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER with reason RIDER_CANCELLED. That reading is accepted, but it does not save the fee, because POL-NS-24 voids it independently.

Contact. The driver made no attempt to reach the rider. The trip record's contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 and call_count 0 with obligation_met false; the chat log holds only the rider's two messages (21:16:40 'Hi, where are you? App shows you not moving' and 21:19:30 'Hello??'), and the only in-app call is the rider's own at 21:20:10, unanswered after 30 s. Because the driver also failed to attempt contact, POL-NS-24's second limb applies on top of the refund: a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is due. Per POL-GEN-03 that credit is a referral naming POL-NS-24, not an escalation, and it never suppresses the money.

The driver's alternative - that the fee stand as DRIVER_COMPENSATION, or that the present state stand as NO_ACTION - is rejected. POL-NS-22 charges the no-show fee when the driver cancels after the free wait; this driver neither arrived nor cancelled. The fee figure itself is correct, so no POL-NS-22 amount referral arises: the ledger's 5.00 SGD equals policy_fee_sgd 5.00 and fee_matches_policy is true. The submission that time and fuel were spent on the booking does not convert a failure to arrive into a no-show the fee can rest on.

The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05056-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3), and no clause in this category turns on traffic data, so its absence neither excuses the non-arrival nor escalates the case. POL-GEN-26 is not engaged: every fact POL-NS-24 and POL-NS-23 need is carried by complete, weight-1.0 artifacts, and no outcome is inferred from any absence here.

The driver's statement ('Passenger cancel herself, why she complain. I was coming.') is noted; it is a bare account contradicted by the driver's own trace and decides nothing.

On POL-NS-25: the rider's profile does not carry no_show_cancellations_30d, so there is no repeat no-show referral. On POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26: the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below 10.00 SGD, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so this AI ruling is final. Confidence is set at 0.90, within the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-24: 5.00 SGD goodwill credit to the rider, the driver having failed to attempt contact before the cancellation.
